claim: Verbalized Sampling (VS) raises diversity in creative writing by 1.6 to 2.1 times over direct prompting.
quote: in creative writing, VS increases diversity by 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting
authors: Zhang, Yu, Chong, Sicilia, Tomz, Manning, Shi
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: Test VS-style 'list several answers with probabilities' as the divergence step in the harness; measure top-k quality, not only spread.

claim: In the VS paper, quality is judged by one LLM judge plus human win rates, and the reported result is 'comparable' quality, not better top outputs. Basic VS and Sequence prompting cost some quality, less on larger models.
quote: Methods like Sequence and VS-Standard do cause a drop in quality
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: Do not assume VS improves the best idea. Use VS-CoT or VS-Multi variants only on strong models and check quality at top-k in our own runs. Only the first 100000 of 234341 characters of the page were read.

claim: The VS paper reports no best-of-n or top-k quality measure for creative tasks in the parts read; its quality evidence is judge scores and human win rates against baselines.
quote: maintains comparable quality win-rates to the baselines
title: Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity
transfer: Gap stays open: we must run our own top-k test.

claim: Across ten LLMs, analogy generation clusters in narrow target domains, and methods that raise diversity often lower quality (a stated trade-off).
quote: increasing output diversity often comes at the expense of output quality
authors: Shen, de Sousa, Barcelos, Guo, Zhu
title: On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models
transfer: Treat diversity boosts as costing quality until shown otherwise; pair every divergence step with a quality filter.

claim: Prompting an LLM to build analogies to cross-domain problems, then search for solutions, raised solution diversity 90 to 173 percent and novel solutions to over 50 percent (baselines as low as 1.6 percent) on four biomedical problems.
title: Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
transfer: Candidate divergence step: analogy to a structurally similar problem in another domain. Abstract does not name baselines or say how novelty and quality were judged; test in our harness.

claim: LLM judges of idea novelty are unstable: telling the judge which idea reviewers found novel can change its verdict on more than half of identical pairs, shifting pairwise accuracy by over 50 points; retrieval and bigger reasoning budgets help little.
quote: can change its verdict on more than half of the identical idea pairs
authors: Sternlicht, Shahid, Jansen, Weld, Siangliulue, Hope
title: Old Ideas, Novel Problems: The Instability of LLM-Based Novelty Evaluation
transfer: Never select the final idea by one LLM judge prompt. Use several prompt variants and different judges, compare with a trivial baseline, and prefer external or executable checks.

claim: When 43 experts executed LLM-made and human-made research ideas, the LLM ideas lost significantly more review score after execution on novelty, excitement, effectiveness and overall, and many human ideas then ranked higher.
title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
transfer: Ideas must pass an execution or feasibility test before they are kept. The abstract was returned as a summary, so no verbatim quote.

claim: In the first Si et al. study, over 100 NLP researchers judged LLM ideas more novel than expert human ideas (p < 0.05) and slightly weaker on feasibility; the abstract lists failures of LLM self-evaluation as an open problem.
title: Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers
transfer: Self-ranking of ideas is a known weak point. Keep an external check. Title taken from memory; page content returned only a summary.

claim: In engineering design (battery pack) LLM agents fixate on existing paradigms like human designers; adding a separate metacognitive co-regulation agent beat self-regulation alone, and both beat a plain loop, at similar compute.
title: Supervising Ralph Wiggum: Exploring a Metacognitive Co-Regulation Agentic AI Loop for Engineering Design
transfer: A second agent that watches for fixation beats self-monitoring. This is a task with a measurable design score, so it avoids an LLM judge. Single problem only.

claim: Separating free divergent candidate generation from a convergent step that selects against task constraints improved divergence of interactive agents over prior methods.
title: Beyond One Path: Evaluating and Enhancing Divergent Thinking in Interactive LLM Agents
transfer: Matches a generate-then-constrained-select step. No numbers retrieved.

claim: In a 48-hour hackathon, ChatGPT-4 placed second of six teams, was strong at concept generation, showed design fixation, and abandoned promising ideas early.
authors: Ege, Ovrebo, Stubberud, Berg, Elverum, Steinert, Vestad
title: ChatGPT as an inventor: Eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
transfer: Keep promising ideas alive through development; do not drop on first difficulty. Read from a search feed summary only.

claim: The same LLM on the same prompt gives outputs from below-average to original; only 0.28 percent of responses reached the top 10 percent of human creativity benchmarks, and the authors advise repeated sampling.
title: Has the Creativity of Large-Language Models peaked? An analysis of inter- and intra-LLM variability
transfer: Within-model variance is large, so sample many and select; that makes the selection method the key part. Tasks are short divergent tests.

claim: Meta-model ensembles (pooling several LLMs plus more inference compute and brainstorming) beat any single model on counts of unique valid scientific ideas; creativity is uneven by model, prompt and field.
title: LLM Jaggedness Unlocks Scientific Creativity
transfer: Pooling across different models adds diversity that one model cannot. Our agent is one LLM, so this is a limit, not a step. Score is count of valid ideas, not quality of the best.

claim: Incubation has a positive effect on problem solving; longer preparation gives a bigger effect; divergent thinking tasks benefit more than insight tasks.
quote: The authors identified a positive incubation effect
title: Does incubation enhance problem solving? A meta-analytic review
n: not stated in the retrieved abstract
transfer: Weak, speculative LLM analogue: revisit a draft in a fresh context after other work. Not tested. Abstract read via Europe PMC record.

claim: In a professional design team, far analogies did not produce ideas distant from the previous ones; ideas were more similar to the preceding ones after far analogies, though the rate of concept generation rose. Authors suggest novelty comes from deep iterative exploration within a functional space.
title: The impact of analogies on creative concept generation: lessons from an in vivo study in engineering design
transfer: Do not treat a far analogy as a one-shot jump. Use it as a seed, then iterate several rounds inside the new functional frame. Europe PMC record gave a summary, not verbatim text; URL is the search page used.

claim: Distant analogies tend to give more innovative solutions, but only up to a point; if stimuli are too distant they hinder design ('there is such a thing as too far'). Near and far are relative.
quote: there is such a thing as too far
authors: Fu, Chan, Cagan, Kotovsky, Schunn, Wood
title: The Meaning of Near and Far: The Impact of Structuring Design Databases and the Effect of Distance of Analogy on Design Output
transfer: Prefer medium-distance analogies; a cap on distance. Quote is from the 2012 conference version abstract as reported by the fetch tool, which called the two abstracts nearly identical.

claim: Sio, Kotovsky and Cagan (2015) is a meta-analytic review of whether examples fixate or inspire designers. I could confirm it exists and its DOI but could not open the abstract or text.
title: Fixation or inspiration? A meta-analytic review of the role of examples on design processes
transfer: none until the text is read. Authors taken from memory; Crossref returned only title, DOI, journal, year.

claim: A review of design-education studies says examples cause fixedness to their features, and that quantity, abstraction, proximity and presentation form (text, photo, diagram, object) change the risk.
quote: examples cause fixedness to their features as a negative effect for creativity
title: Examples in Design Education: Inspiration or Fixation?
transfer: Show abstract rather than concrete examples when examples are used.

claim: Idea-Catalyst, which pulls in insights from other disciplines, raised average novelty by 21 percent and insightfulness by 16 percent; the abstract does not say whether judges were human or LLM.
quote: improves average novelty by 21% and insightfulness by 16%
title: Sparking Scientific Creativity via LLM-Driven Interdisciplinary Inspiration
transfer: Cross-field retrieval as a divergence step. Judge type unknown, so weak.

claim: A re-examination of min-p sampling found the original evidence does not show gains over baseline samplers in quality or diversity.
title: Min-p, Max Exaggeration: A Critical Analysis of Min-p Sampling in Language Models
transfer: Supports holding sampler-level diversity claims loosely. Seen only as a one-line feed summary.

claim: A tournament-based relative ranking of candidate thinking flows is used to favor higher-quality ones; the abstract gives no baselines or numbers.
title: MindFlow: Mind Supernet Powered Thinking Flows for Research Idea Innovation
transfer: Pairwise tournaments exist as a selection design, but no evidence of benefit retrieved.

claim: CHECK: Does diversity boosting improve the BEST output, not only spread? UNSETTLED. The VS paper reports diversity gains and 'comparable' quality, uses one LLM judge, and shows quality drops for basic VS. A separate preprint states diversity methods often cost quality. No top-k or best-of-n test and no independent replication of VS found.
transfer: Run our own test: score the best of k outputs under VS, persona and plain sampling on a task with an external score.

claim: CHECK: Selection by LLM self-ranking or single LLM judge is unreliable. SUPPORTED (preprints). Sternlicht 2026 shows prompt wording flips verdicts; Si 2024 lists self-evaluation failure; Si 2025 shows judged novelty did not survive execution. No work found that proves a tournament or diverse judge panel fixes this. Execution-based or external verification is the only option with some support (Xu 2026 used a measured design score).
transfer: Selection order: executable or external check first, then multi-prompt multi-judge panel as a weak filter.

claim: CHECK: Ward 1994 path of least resistance replication or meta-analysis. NOT SETTLED. No replication or newer meta-analysis found. Web search budget ran out before this query, so only a Semantic Scholar attempt was made and it failed with HTTP 429. Treat Ward as one old study.
transfer: none

claim: CHECK: Far analogies help novelty. CONTESTED, with a boundary. Fu 2013 says distant helps up to a point and too far hurts; Chan and Schunn 2015 found ideas closer to the previous ones after far analogies, though output rate rose. Both are small design studies. Rule: medium distance and iterate.
transfer: Analogy step: medium-distance source, then several refinement rounds.

claim: CHECK: Incubation replication or newer meta-analysis. NOT FOUND. One Europe PMC query for recent work returned 2026 items on aha moments, mind wandering and set shifting, none a meta-analysis or direct replication. Sio and Ormerod 2009 remains the single meta-analysis. No LLM analogue of incubation (revisiting drafts after a context reset) was found in an arXiv query. One search per topic only, so absence is weak.
transfer: Treat revisit-after-reset as an untested idea, cheap to try in the harness.

claim: CHECK: When to switch divergence off on convergent tasks. NOT SETTLED. Found no source that gives a task-type gate. Park et al. 2026 split divergent generation from constrained selection, which is a structure, not a gate. Our own ARC and word-puzzle results remain the only evidence.
transfer: Build the gate ourselves and test it: classify the task first, run divergence only on open-ended ones.

claim: CHECK: Expert creative-process studies of scientists and designers with controlled tests on LLM agents (reformulation, constraint relaxation, blending). NOT FOUND in controlled form. Found only tools (PopBlends, a human-in-the-loop blending system) and the Ralph Wiggum design-fixation agent loop. Search budget limited this to arXiv queries.
transfer: none yet
